technical_and_design_decisions: Count-based deployment properties (U1) will leverage Spring's existing PropertyPlaceholderConfigurer/PropertySourcesPlaceholderConfigurer mechanism, extending the deployment property resolver to recognize a dedicated 'count' token and instantiate N copies of the module with shared environment variables.

gh-pages branch (U2) will be configured as an orphan branch using the standard GitHub Pages approach; documentation generation will be wired into the existing Maven/Gradle build with Asciidoctor or MkDocs output, published via a CI job that pushes generated HTML to gh-pages.

Kafka binder fix (U3) will be approached as a targeted bug fix in the spring-cloud-stream-binder-kafka module, with diagnostic logging added first to confirm the binding failure mode before code changes; backward compatibility with existing Kafka client versions will be preserved.

Architecture reference documentation (U4) will be written in AsciiDoc and structured as a side-by-side comparison of 1.x and 2.x deployment topologies (local, Cloud Foundry, Kubernetes, Yarn), leveraging the existing reference guide template.

Concourse CI study (U5) is scoped as a research task: explore pipelines, tasks, resources, and fly CLI; produce a written findings document with recommendations; no production pipeline implementation is included.

RxJava processor module (U6) will follow the existing Spring Cloud Stream processor pattern (Function/Consumer/Supplier) and use RxJava's Flowable/Observable adapters; the module will be a thin wrapper around the reactive-stream contract to avoid duplicating binder code.
Shell server banner (U7) will be generated as ASCII art via patorjk.com/taag, stored as a banner.txt resource, and wired into the Spring Boot Banner mechanism via spring.main.banner-location.
Cloud Foundry deployment section (U8) will be added to the project README following the existing section structure, with concrete steps and a link to the canonical docs.

All activities assume a single senior developer working full-time; code review, unit tests, and minor integration verification are folded into each activity's estimate rather than treated as a separate line item.
assumptions: {{count}}, {{N}}, {{gh_pages}}, and {{Kafka}} are template variables from the story tracker; the intended values are 'count' (property name), N (an integer count of instances), 'gh-pages' (branch name), and 'Kafka' (the Kafka binder for Spring Cloud Stream).

The Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d) and Spring Cloud Stream / Spring Cloud Stream Microservices (s-c-s / s-c-s-m) codebases, build infrastructure, and CI are already in place; no bootstrapping of repos, build systems, or environments is required.
An 8-hour workday is used as the unit of effort; estimates are effort (person-days), not calendar duration.
U5 (Concourse CI study) is treated as a research-and-document deliverable, not an implementation; it therefore requires a shorter time than the coding stories.
No large-scale refactoring, breaking API changes, or new framework subsystems are implied by the stories; each story fits within the existing architecture.
The Kafka binder bug is of moderate complexity (not a fundamental redesign); if the actual bug proves deeper, estimates would need to be revised upward.
Documentation is published using the project's existing static-site/doc generation toolchain; no new doc-system selection is required.

activities.activity_description: Define the property syntax (e.g., deployer.<module>.count=N), the substitution rules, and how the resolved count propagates through the deployment launcher to spawn N module instances sharing the same environment variables.
Extend the deployment property resolver, update the module deployment path to iterate N times while sharing env vars, and wire the new property through the relevant configurers/listeners.
Add unit and integration tests covering count=1, count>1, count with shared env vars, and invalid count values; verify the launcher creates the correct number of module instances.
Create the orphan gh-pages branch in the s-c-d and s-c-s-m repositories, set up the branch as the GitHub Pages source, and add a README placeholder so the page renders correctly.
Configure the build to generate HTML docs and a CI job (Travis/CircleCI) that pushes the generated output to the gh-pages branch on merge to main.
Reproduce the binding failure against an operational Kafka broker, capture broker/client logs, and isolate the root cause within the spring-cloud-stream-binder-kafka module.
Apply the targeted code change to address the diagnosed issue, preserving compatibility with supported Kafka client versions and existing configuration properties.
Add regression tests for the fixed scenario, run the binder test suite against a live or testcontainers-based Kafka broker, and verify successful binding.
Review both codebases, identify the key structural differences (server, skipper, deployers, stream DSL, batch/task handling), and outline the comparison structure.
Author the AsciiDoc reference page describing 1.x and 2.x deployment differences, with diagrams (PlantUML) and concrete examples for each target platform.
Explore Concourse CI concepts (pipelines, tasks, resources, jobs, the fly CLI), review sample pipelines, and evaluate fit for s-c-d's CI/CD needs.
Produce a written summary covering capabilities, integration options, migration effort, and recommendations for adopting Concourse CI in s-c-d.
Define the module's API surface (function signatures, RxJava Flowable/Observable types), its relationship to the spring-cloud-stream reactive binder, and configuration properties.
Implement the processor module with adapters between RxJava types and the reactive-streams contract used by Spring Cloud Stream, register it as a Spring configuration class.
Write unit and integration tests verifying the RxJava processor correctly publishes/subscribes through the binder, including back-pressure and error-propagation cases.

activities.activity_description: Add a 'Running on Cloud Foundry' section to the s-c-d README, covering prerequisites, manifest, deployment steps, and a link to the detailed docs.
